question_text:
Two mercury-in-glass thermometers $P$ and $Q$ are to be constructed with $P$ having a larger bulb of the same material as that of $Q$ but with twice the volume of $Q$. Assume that the walls of both bulbs have the same thickness. Consider the following statements:
Using capillary tubes with appropriate uniform bore radii, the two thermometers can be constructed to have the same capillary length between $0^\circ C$ and $100^\circ C$ markings.

options.option_text: A higher sensitivity in thermometer $P$ than in measuring temperature.
the same response time for rapid changes in the sensitivity of $Q$ thermometer.
Only A and C are true.
A, B and C are true.
